title: Approval notification sent despite user disabling all notifications
gherkin:
Feature: Mandatory Notification Exception Handling

Scenario: Approval-related notification bypasses user preference settings
  Given a user has disabled all notification types in their preferences
  And a rental approval event occurs
  When the system processes the approval notification
  Then the approval notification shall be sent to the user
  And the notification shall not be filtered by user preference settings
rationale: Validates that business-critical approval notifications are treated as mandatory exceptions and are sent regardless of user preference settings. This addresses the core exception requirement that approval-related notifications may need to remain non-optional despite user preference configuration.
usedContextItems: System shall allow users to configure notification preferences and enable/disable specific notification types|Some approval-related notification messages may need to remain non-optional despite user preference settings (business-critical events)

From: marketing@toolchain.com
Date: 2026-02-26 16:00
Subject: Question about promotional content in reminder communications

Hi Team,

For the beta period, Marketing would like to explore whether reminder-style emails could also carry a small promotional or onboarding message, instead of treating product messaging and operational reminders as completely separate streams.

Before we move in that direction, we need guidance on how this should interact with user notification settings. From a campaign perspective, the reminder channel looks attractive because it already reaches active users at important points in the rental journey. However, we do not want to assume that a message containing both operational and promotional content should automatically follow the same preference rules as a purely operational reminder.

Please advise whether this needs a dedicated notification category, a separate consent decision, or a strict separation between transactional and promotional messaging.

Best,
Marketing Dept.

From: logistics_manager@toolchain.com
Date: 2026-02-22 11:00
Subject: Warehouse handling concern for item identifiers

Hi All,

During the warehouse pilot, the team raised a usability concern around how item identifiers are handled on labels and during scanning.

In daily operations, staff tend to refer to the machine-readable identifier as the barcode or serial code rather than by the formal term used in the specification. The current business-oriented format may be less convenient for the scanning workflow than a more scanner-friendly representation.

For now, please review whether the warehouse-facing identifier should remain just an operational alias in the UI, or whether a separate machine-readable identifier is needed alongside the formal item identifier. The main goal is to reduce ambiguity for staff and avoid slowing down intake and return handling.

Thanks,
Gary (Logistics)

resolutionNotes: TARGET R61c addresses mandatory notification exception handling. PRIMARY evidence establishes core notification requirements (lifecycle events, delivery, preferences, logging) and identifies a critical policy ambiguity: whether approval-related or business-critical notifications should bypass user preference filtering. E3 and E9 explicitly flag this as unresolved. CONTEXT evidence (E13-E16) indicates related preference rule refinements and gaps around promotional content mixing and preference enforcement, but these are supporting context rather than direct target specifications. The operative context captures the baseline notification behavior; exceptions capture the unresolved mandatory/non-optional distinction; gaps capture dependencies on undefined policy decisions and configuration thresholds. Thanks,
Gary (Logistics)

Subject: Question about promotional content in reminder communications

Hi Team,

For the beta period, Marketing would like to explore whether reminder-style emails could also carry a small promotional or onboarding message, instead of treating product messaging and operational reminders as completely separate streams.

Before we move in that direction, we need guidance on how this should interact with user notification settings. From a campaign perspective, the reminder channel looks attractive because it already reaches active users at important points in the rental journey. However, we do not want to assume that a message containing both operational and promotional content should automatically follow the same preference rules as a purely operational reminder.

Please advise whether this needs a dedicated notification category, a separate consent decision, or a strict separation between transactional and promotional messaging.

Best,
Marketing Dept.

Subject: Warehouse handling concern for item identifiers

Hi All,

During the warehouse pilot, the team raised a usability concern around how item identifiers are handled on labels and during scanning.

In daily operations, staff tend to refer to the machine-readable identifier as the barcode or serial code rather than by the formal term used in the specification. The current business-oriented format may be less convenient for the scanning workflow than a more scanner-friendly representation.

For now, please review whether the warehouse-facing identifier should remain just an operational alias in the UI, or whether a separate machine-readable identifier is needed alongside the formal item identifier. The main goal is to reduce ambiguity for staff and avoid slowing down intake and return handling.

Thanks,
Gary (Logistics)

generationSummary: Test suite for R61c: Mandatory notification exception handling. These tests validate that the system correctly handles exceptions to standard user notification preferences, specifically for business-critical and approval-related notifications that must remain non-optional. Tests cover scenarios where approval notifications bypass user preference filtering, administrative notifications to authorized users are exempt from standard filtering, and the interaction between mandatory exceptions and configurable user preferences.
resolvedOperativeContext: System shall send reminder notifications before rent start and end dates with configurable timing || System shall allow users to configure notification preferences and enable/disable specific notification types || ## 5.3.1 The system shall send reminder notifications before rent start date. || Notification content shall include item identifier, rental period, and rent status || System shall apply user notification preferences when sending notifications
resolvedExceptions: Some approval-related notification messages may need to remain non-optional despite user preference settings (business-critical events) || Administrative notifications to authorized users may not be subject to standard user preference filtering
resolutionNotes: TARGET R61c addresses mandatory notification exception handling. PRIMARY evidence establishes core notification requirements (lifecycle events, delivery, preferences, logging) and identifies a critical policy ambiguity: whether approval-related or business-critical notifications should bypass user preference filtering. E3 and E9 explicitly flag this as unresolved. CONTEXT evidence (E13-E16) indicates related preference rule refinements and gaps around promotional content mixing and preference enforcement, but these are supporting context rather than direct target specifications. The operative context captures the baseline notification behavior; exceptions capture the unresolved mandatory/non-optional distinction; gaps capture dependencies on undefined policy decisions and configuration thresholds. Filtered abstract or low-relevance operative statements: System shall generate notifications for rent lifecycle events (creation, approval, rejection, Active, Completed, Cancelled) | System shall send notifications via email to the user account email address | System shall ensure notification delivery is reliable with retry support on failure
